Give the app the three permissions it asks for. Then, on the Shares tab, add your NAS or server: its address, the share or export on it, and your user and password; Test the connection says whether it works. Last, on the Shuttles tab, Add a shuttle: it walks through the share, the folder on it and what of it to sync, the folder on the phone, a profile, and the settings.
What are shares, shuttles and profiles?

A share is a server and the folder it shares: SMB (Windows, Samba, most NAS), NFS, or a folder already on the phone. A shuttle is one folder on the phone and one on a share, kept in step. A profile is a set of settings that shuttles share, so that changing it changes them all; a shuttle can still set any one of them itself.

↑ Push copies what changes on the phone to the share: a backup of your photos, say. ↓ Pull copies what changes on the share to the phone. ⇅ Sync goes both ways. Push and pull never delete on the other side unless Deletions is mirror; sync deletes on both sides what is deleted on one.

When you tap Sync now, and as its Triggers say: realtime, as files change, with a notification up while it watches; schedule, every so often or at set times, which Android runs around the time asked, not to the minute; share-available, when the share can be reached again.
Can a shuttle sync only some of the folder?

Yes: on the wizard\'s \"What to sync in it\" step, choose \"Only what is marked\" or \"All but what is marked\", and tick files and folders. A folder partly ticked has something inside it marked. Ignore, in the settings, leaves out names by pattern, such as *.tmp.

It says why under its name: a permission the app does not have (All files access, local network), a share that cannot be reached, or a metered connection, such as a phone\'s hotspot, which shuttles wait out unless their Metered setting is run.
What happens when a file changed on both sides?

By default, both are kept: the older beside the newer, under a name that says where it came from. With Conflicts set to ask, the shuttle waits for you on the Conflicts tab: keep the phone\'s, the share\'s, or both.

When a run would delete more than the Guard\'s share of the files at once (half, by default), none are deleted: a folder that went missing looks the same. Check both folders, then allow them on the Conflicts tab.
Where do replaced and deleted files go?
Into a .shuttle-versions folder inside the shuttle\'s folder, on the side that changed, for 30 days by default. Versions, in the settings, keeps them longer, keeps the last few, or none.
Why were some files left out?
The phone\'s storage cannot hold names with : ? * \" < > | or \\, which a share can. Such files are listed on the shuttle\'s screen as left out, and are never deleted on the share for it.
In the app, encrypted with a key that never leaves the phone\'s Android Keystore. They are not in the config file, and not in a backup.

Force-stopping the app, in Android\'s settings, stops all of its syncing until it is opened again; the app says so when it is. A battery saver that restricts the app can delay what it runs in the background.

shuttle needs three permissions to sync. You can give them now or later; until you do, the shuttles that need one wait and say which.
To read and write the folders you sync in the phone\'s storage. Without it, shuttles with a folder there wait, and nothing in them is synced or deleted.
To reach your NAS or other computers on your network. Without it, Android lets those connections time out, and shuttles with a share there wait.
To tell you about errors, conflicts and finished syncs, and to show while syncing runs. Without them, shuttle still syncs, silently.
